title: FLIR1 "Tic Tac" (F/A-18F, ATFLIR, USS Nimitz group, November 2004)
summary: Forensic reconstruction of FLIR1 "Tic Tac" (F/A-18F, ATFLIR, USS Nimitz group, November 2004): the jet path, line of sight and field of view per frame, scored against each candidate explanation with identical geometry and weights.

environment.note: Wind at the object's altitude carries this uncertainty for every hypothesis.

analysis.method: Maximum-likelihood multi-start fit per hypothesis; BIC-style complexity penalty; same code and weights for all.
analysis.log_likelihood_note: Natural log; higher is better; a difference of 2.3 is a likelihood ratio of 10.

hypotheses.label: Distant aircraft (engine exhaust seen as glare)
hypotheses.priors_summary: An ordinary aircraft (airliner or military jet) at cruise altitude and speed, whose hot engine exhaust saturates the infrared sensor. The blob is a glare: its size follows its brightness rather than the range, and its orientation follows the pod's derotation. Priors: range_ref_nmi loguniform [0.5, 60.0]; airspeed_kt uniform [250.0, 520.0]; heading_deg uniform [0.0, 360.0]; vz_fpm normal [-4000.0, 4000.0].

checks.source: A glare's size says nothing about the airframe; not checked.

hypotheses.label: Sensor artifact (glare in the pod optics) on a target of any type
hypotheses.priors_summary: What the camera shows is a glare in the pod's own optics; its orientation is set by the pod's derotation and its size by its brightness. Behind the glare is a real target of any type, at any range and speed, whose path the line of sight follows. Priors: range_ref_nmi loguniform [0.5, 60.0]; airspeed_kt uniform [0.0, 600.0]; heading_deg uniform [0.0, 360.0]; vz_fpm normal [-4000.0, 4000.0].

checks.source: A glare's size says nothing about the target; not checked.

hypotheses.label: Balloon drifting with the wind
hypotheses.priors_summary: A balloon (party, research or other) carried by the wind at its altitude. It has no speed through the air of its own; it may rise or sink slowly. Its apparent speed in the video is parallax: the jet's own motion against a nearly still object. Priors: range_ref_nmi loguniform [0.5, 60.0]; vz_fpm normal [-2000.0, 2000.0].

checks.source: S3: party and small weather balloons are 0.3 to 2 m across; the blob length is an upper bound (it includes the optics' blur).

hypotheses.label: Close small object
hypotheses.priors_summary: A small object (bird, small drone, balloon or debris) within 2 nmi of the jet, much closer than it looks. Small size and nearness trade off: a close small object and a distant large one subtend the same angle. Priors: range_ref_nmi loguniform [0.05, 2.0]; airspeed_kt uniform [0.0, 80.0]; heading_deg uniform [0.0, 360.0]; vz_fpm normal [-2000.0, 2000.0].

checks.source: Design table: size 0.1 to 2 m. Reported as a check (the normalized size trend cannot see absolute size); the blob length is an upper bound.

hypotheses.label: Slow object (bird or small drone)
hypotheses.priors_summary: A slow flier, such as a bird or a small drone, at whatever range the data imply. It moves through the air at up to 60 kt in any direction and is carried by the wind; its apparent speed in the video is mostly parallax from the jet's motion. Priors: range_ref_nmi loguniform [0.5, 60.0]; airspeed_kt uniform [0.0, 60.0]; heading_deg uniform [0.0, 360.0]; vz_fpm normal [-2000.0, 2000.0].

checks.source: S1, S2: birds 0.1 to 2 m wingspan, small drones 0.2 to 0.6 m; the blob length is an upper bound.

hypotheses.label: Object on a free path (no physical model)
hypotheses.priors_summary: An object with no physical model at all: a smooth path with no speed limit, at any range from 0.5 to 60 nmi. It shows what the geometry alone requires, and what the aircrew's statements (scored as testimony, the same way for every hypothesis) then add. Its flexibility is charged by the complexity penalty like any other free parameter. Priors: range_ref_nmi loguniform [0.5, 60.0].

checks.source: No physical model, so no size expectation; sizes claimed by witnesses are scored by the testimony criterion.

range_curves.note: Angles-only curves: for each assumed constant range, the speed, altitude and fit that the line-of-sight angles imply. Range is not measured in this clip's angles; read the curve, not one number. Per-hypothesis curves over range are not in the current outputs.

testimony.claims_summary: 108 claims from 12 witnesses or records; 14 constrain a quantity the models predict (18 scored terms). Each is a paraphrase with a source; testimony is applied identically to every hypothesis.

witness_consistency.note: Memory of on-screen numbers against the record; reported separately and never changes a score.

verdict.text: On the video alone (physics-only), Object on a free path (no physical model) scores highest, ahead of the next explanation by 34.3 log units, but this is not called decisive: with a rotation noise above 12.75 deg (the data-only value is 11.86 deg) H-ART leads instead; in the model-recovery test, data made by H-CLOSE were also won by H-WIT, so this data cannot tell those explanations apart.
conditions: Range is not measured in this clip; conclusions hold over the stated range support (0.5 to 60 nmi), not at one range.
Scores are log-likelihoods under the lab's noise model; a gap of 2.3 is a likelihood ratio of 10.
Every hypothesis is fitted by the same code against the same observables with the same noise model and weights; hypotheses differ only in their physical model and priors.
No data-quality exclusion applies to this case; every criterion carries its full weight.
Sensitivity: with a rotation noise above 12.75 deg (the data-only value is 11.86 deg) H-ART leads instead.
Sensitivity: in the model-recovery test, data made by H-CLOSE were also won by H-WIT, so this data cannot tell those explanations apart.
